extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, distributors, researchers, registrants, and legal/regulatory stakeholders affected by DEA controlled-substance scheduling
extracted.subtask_description: Final DEA rulemaking placing 4-fluoroamphetamine (4-FA) in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, describing legal authority, HHS/DEA analyses, public comments, scheduling findings, and handling/ compliance requirements for registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority and statutory procedure for scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory procedures under 21 U.S.C. 811(a), (b), and (d) govern adding or transferring a drug to a schedule; the Secretary of HHS consults with the Attorney General and the Attorney General (delegated to the DEA Administrator) may, by rule and upon the recommendation of the Secretary, add to a schedule if she finds the substance has a potential for abuse and makes the findings prescribed by 21 U.S.C. 812(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 21 U.S.C. 811(d)(2)-(4), 811(a)(1)-(2), and 812(b) and explains that when UN scheduling notifications occur, the Secretary must first determine whether existing controls meet treaty requirements; if consultation/temporary order procedures are not followed, permanent scheduling procedures at 21 U.S.C. 811(a)-(b) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eight‑factor analysis under 21 U.S.C. 811(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA conducted its own analysis under the eight factors stipulated in 21 U.S.C. 811(c) and reviewed HHS's scientific and medical evaluation and scheduling recommendation pursuant to 21 U.S.C. 811(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEA and HHS Eight-Factor Analyses are relied upon as primary scientific/medical bases for scheduling and are available in the public docket (DEA-1180). The eight factors determine substance abuse potential, pharmacology, public health risks, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory findings required for Schedule I placement
rubrics_metrics.description: To place a substance in Schedule I, the Administrator must find that the substance: (1) has a high potential for abuse, (2) has no currently accepted medical use in treatment in the United States, and (3) lacks accepted safety for use under medical supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEA applied 21 U.S.C. 812(b)(1) to 4-FA and made these three explicit findings as substantial evidence to warrant Schedule I control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑part test for 'currently accepted medical use' (traditional DEA test)
rubrics_metrics.description: When no FDA approval exists, DEA traditionally applies a five-part test to determine currently accepted medical use: (1) the drug's chemistry must be known and reproducible; (2) there must be adequate safety studies; (3) there must be adequate and well-controlled studies proving efficacy; (4) the drug must be accepted by qualified experts; and (5) the scientific evidence must be widely available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEA and HHS applied this five-part test to 4-FA and concluded it was not satisfied. Case law and prior Federal Register citations (e.g., Marijuana Scheduling Petition) inform application of this test.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS alternative two‑part test for currently accepted medical use (when five‑part test not satisfied)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS has applied an additional two-part test for substances failing the five-part test: (1) whether there exists widespread, current experience with medical use of the substance by licensed health care practitioners operating in accordance with jurisdiction-authorized programs recognized by medical regulatory entities, and (2) whether there exists some credible scientific support for at least one of the medical conditions for which part (1) is satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department of Justice Office of Legal Counsel opined the HHS two-part test would be sufficient to establish currently accepted medical use; DEA noted no evidence that these two-part test conditions are met for 4-FA.

rubrics_metrics.name: International treaty obligation (1971 Convention) as scheduling criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the United States is a party to the 1971 Convention on Psychotropic Substances, when the CND places a substance on an international schedule the U.S. must place appropriate controls to meet the minimum requirements of the treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule notes that scheduling 4-FA in the CSA is in part to enable the U.S. to meet obligations under the 1971 Convention and explains procedural implications when international scheduling notifications occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) and opportunity for hearing/comments
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA published an NPRM proposing permanent control of 4-FA in Schedule I, provided an opportunity to file requests for hearing and to submit comments by a specified deadline, and reported it received no hearing requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural compliance includes publishing an NPRM, setting deadlines for hearing requests and comments (e.g., July 3, 2025), and following the administrative rulemaking procedures 'on the record after opportunity for a hearing' under 5 U.S.C. 556 and 557 where required by 21 U.S.C. 811(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and response to public comments
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA received nine comments (two supportive, five opposed, two neutral) and summarized the substantive points (e.g., claims about existing analogue coverage, research impact, potential therapeutic uses). DEA considered these comments but relied on HHS scientific/medical evaluation and its eight‑factor analysis in concluding substantial evidence of potential for abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEA's responses clarify legal/technical positions (e.g., 4-FA was not previously scheduled under the CSA, treaty obligations require scheduling, Schedule I placement does not preclude research but requires DEA permission). The weight given to comments depends on scientific/medical evidence and statutory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Registration to handle 4-FA
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who handles (manufactures, distributes, reverse distributes, imports, exports, engages in research, conducts instructional activities or chemical analysis with, or possesses), or who desires to handle, 4-FA must register with DEA pursuant to 21 U.S.C. 822, 823, 957, and 958, and in accordance with 21 CFR parts 1301 and 1312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons currently handling 4-FA and not registered must submit an application and may not continue to handle 4-FA unless DEA approves the registration. Retail sales of Schedule I substances to the general public are not allowed; unauthorized possession is unlawful and prosecutable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Disposal or transfer of existing stocks prior to effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons unwilling or unable to obtain a Schedule I registration must surrender or transfer all quantities of currently held 4-FA to a DEA-registered person before the effective date, in accordance with applicable Federal, State, local, and Tribal laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4-FA must be disposed of in accordance with 21 CFR part 1317 and all other applicable laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Security for handling and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: 4-FA is subject to Schedule I security requirements and must be handled and stored pursuant to 21 U.S.C. 823 and in accordance with 21 CFR 1301.71–1301.76; non-practitioners must comply with employee screening requirements at 21 CFR 1301.90–1301.93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security measures and employee screening requirements applicable to Schedule I substances apply as of the effective date of the scheduling action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Labeling and packaging compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All labels, labeling, and packaging for commercial containers of 4-FA must comply with 21 U.S.C. 825 and be in accordance with 21 CFR part 1302.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must follow statutory labeling/packaging requirements applicable to controlled substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Manufacturing quota controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally only registered manufacturers are permitted to manufacture 4-FA in accordance with a quota assigned pursuant to 21 U.S.C. 826 and in accordance with 21 CFR part 1303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production of 4-FA is subject to DEA quotas and applicable quota regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Inventory obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Every DEA registrant who possesses any quantity of 4-FA must take an inventory on hand pursuant to 21 U.S.C. 827 and in accordance with 21 CFR 1304.03, 1304.04, and 1304.11(a) and (d); initial inventory required upon first engaging in handling, and biennial inventories thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial inventory rules and biennial inventory frequency are specified; citations to the relevant CFR provisions are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Records and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Every DEA registrant must maintain records and submit reports for 4-FA or products containing 4-FA pursuant to 21 U.S.C. 827 and in accordance with 21 CFR 1301.74(b) and (c), 1301.76(b), and parts 1304, 1312 and 1317. Manufacturers and distributors must report to ARCOS where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must be submitted to the Automated Reports and Consolidated Ordering System (ARCOS) pursuant to 21 U.S.C. 827 and 21 CFR parts 1304 and 1312.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Order form compliance for distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA registrants who distribute 4-FA must comply with order form requirements pursuant to 21 U.S.C. 828 and 21 CFR part 1305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controlled substance order forms and recordkeeping for orders are required for distribution of 4-FA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Importation and exportation controls
rubrics_metrics.description: All importation and exportation of 4-FA must comply with 21 U.S.C. 952, 953, 957, and 958, and in accordance with 21 CFR parts 1304 and 1312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customs, licensing, and reporting requirements for international movement of controlled substances apply to 4-FA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for unauthorized activities involving 4-FA
rubrics_metrics.description: Any activity involving 4-FA not authorized by, or in violation of, the CSA or its implementing regulations is unlawful and may subject the person to administrative, civil, and/or criminal sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlawful possession, manufacture, distribution, import/export, or other handling without proper authorization can trigger enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory analyses – Executive Orders determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule discusses applicability/exemption from Executive Orders 12866, 13563, 14192, and 14294 and states DEA scheduling actions are exempt from OMB review under E.O. 12866 and not subject to E.O. 14192 or 14294.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule asserts it meets standards of E.O. 12988 (Civil Justice Reform) to eliminate drafting errors and ambiguity and discusses Federalism (E.O. 13132) and Tribal implications (E.O. 13175), concluding no substantial direct effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator certifies under the Regulatory Flexibility Act (5 U.S.C. 601–612) that this final rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEA explains reasons (e.g., no legitimate marketed drug sources in U.S., limited impact on small entities) supporting the certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: This action does not impose a new collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act; however, it requires compliance with existing OMB collections (list of control numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may not conduct/sponsor collections without valid OMB control numbers; the rule references existing OMB collection numbers that apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under UMRA, DEA determined the action would not result in any Federal mandate resulting in aggregate expenditures of $100,000,000 or more in any 1 year; therefore, no Small Government Agency Plan or other action is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UMRA threshold and requirement references are provided to justify lack of additional obligations under UMRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule is not a 'major rule' as defined by the CRA, but DEA will submit a copy of the rule to both Houses of Congress and to the Comptroller General pursuant to the CRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates procedural step of CRA filing even where the rule is not considered 'major.'
